newsitem.title: UK: Supply pressures weaken EU grains but Germany firm.
newsitem.headline: Supply pressures weaken EU grains but Germany firm.

text.p: European grain prices slipped further this week on abundant supplies except in Germany where they advanced on steady demand from eastern Europe.
New arrivals of maize tamed an otherwise tight market, pressuring high prices in France, Italy and Spain. A large Saudi deal and lack of farm output kept barley firm.

Traders anxiously awaited to see if the European Union (EU) would award substantial wheat tonnages in Thursday's export tender to prevent further price drops at home. A review of malt export refund was also expected.
German wheat sellers kept their quotes high on the grounds that more business with eastern Europe was anticipated.
"Poland has bought bread wheat at 290 marks/tonne and there is now talk of Uzbekistan business," one said.
The milling industry was well covered and shopping around for 285 marks elsewhere in Europe for small volumes.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week raised its new crop bread wheat price (12.5 percent) by 2.50 marks to 287.50, reversing last week's reduction, but buyers were 10 marks lower.
French dealers meanwhile blamed thin export prospects for an overall weakening in prices.
"Wheat is hurt by a lack of fresh business even if sellers are still reluctant to lower their prices," one dealer said.
But Thursday's large wheat export bids of 591,250 tonnes offered some support with wheat into Rouen for Oct-Dec delivery standing unchanged from last week at 875 francs after having slipped to 870.
New maize was arriving steadily after last week's rain which had slowed down the cuttings in the southwest. Bordeaux maize for Oct-Dec delivery eased 10 francs to 880 francs.

New crop was also coming on the market in northern Spain, creating some pressure there. With French supplies entering at 25,500 to 25,800 pesetas, traders were seeing October delivery offers at 24,500 and expecting further price drops.
Harvesting was behind schedule in Italy but prices were stable.

UK feed wheat suffered fresh losses this week on continued farm selling and concern that supply may outstrip demand. Good export business was reported with Italy and Spain, where regional delivery is slow, but order books were dry after November. "There is an awful lot in the market and sterling is strong," said one trader. "Noone has any confidence in the forward demand."
But traders said they expected the market to find a bottom soon as farmers would refuse selling if prices went below the current ex-farm level of 100 stg.
Italian soft wheat was unchanged but durum eased some 3,000 lire from last week.
"There continues to be a good amount of supply, but there is a general lack of interest," one dealer said.
Transport problems continued to push up delivered wheat prices in Spain as the sugar beet harvest placed trucks in short supply.
Barley was a touch weaker in central regions where buyers were well-stocked.
